name: human_sessions
description: Server-managed browser session: an opaque cookie credential's hash, its bounds and assurance, and the sealed provider tokens obtained for it.
lifecycle: Created at login as ACTIVE, or PENDING_LIMIT when the principal already has five active sessions; REVOKED rows are retained without deletion until a retention rule is approved under PH-13.

columns.Meaning: Backend-generated session UUID, shown to its owner for session management and bound into sealed tokens and CSRF tokens.
SHA-256 of the 32-byte random cookie credential; the recoverable credential is never stored.
PENDING_LIMIT may only list and end sessions; ACTIVE may call protected operations; REVOKED is terminal.
Provider session identifier (OIDC sid) used to apply back-channel logout.
columns.Null meaning: The provider did not report a session identifier.

columns.Meaning: Authentication context class (acr) asserted by the ID token verified at login.
Provider-reported instant of the user's authentication (auth_time) for this session, used for recent-authentication checks (at most five minutes old for sensitive operations).

Retired: instant of a teluni-aal2 step-up under the former mandatory two-step policy. Since two-step verification became optional for each person, the API neither writes nor reads it; recent-authentication checks use authenticated_at. Kept until a reviewed contract migration removes it.
columns.Null meaning: Every session created since two-step verification became optional, and earlier sessions without a step-up.

columns.Meaning: Inactivity bound applied to this session: 1800 for administrative contexts or principals without memberships, 7200 for operator-only access.
PostgreSQL-clock instant the session was created.
PostgreSQL-clock instant of the latest recorded human activity; background requests do not advance it, and writes are throttled to 15 seconds.
Instant after which the session is invalid regardless of activity, at most 12 hours after creation.
Provider access, refresh and ID tokens sealed with AES-256-GCM under the session key ring and bound to the session ID.
Database-clock estimate of the sealed access token's expiry, five seconds earlier than the provider's lifetime.
Latest instant the provider confirmed the session through introspection, refresh or login.
End of the single-flight lease held by the request refreshing provider tokens.
PostgreSQL-clock instant the session was revoked.
columns.Null meaning: The session has not been revoked.

columns.Meaning: Why the session ended: logout, user termination, expiry, replacement, provider logout or inactivity, refresh rejection, principal disablement or principal mismatch.
columns.Null meaning: The session has not been revoked.

constraints.Purpose: Absolute expiry follows creation by at most the selected 12-hour maximum.
Inactivity bound stays between one minute and the two-hour operator maximum.

constraints.Physical definition: FOREIGN KEY (principal_id) REFERENCES principals(id) ON UPDATE RESTRICT ON DELETE RESTRICT
constraints.Purpose: A session belongs to an existing principal; principals cannot be deleted while sessions exist.

constraints.Physical definition: CHECK (((revocation_reason IS NULL) OR ((revocation_reason)::text = ANY ((ARRAY['LOGOUT'::character varying, 'TERMINATED_BY_USER'::character varying, 'EXPIRED'::character varying, 'REPLACED'::character varying, 'PROVIDER_LOGOUT'::character varying, 'PROVIDER_INACTIVE'::character varying, 'REFRESH_REJECTED'::character varying, 'PRINCIPAL_DISABLED'::character varying, 'PRINCIPAL_MISMATCH'::character varying])::text[]))))
constraints.Purpose: Revocation reason is one of the documented values.

constraints.Physical definition: CHECK (((state = 'REVOKED'::"HumanSessionState") = ((revoked_at IS NOT NULL) AND (revocation_reason IS NOT NULL))))
constraints.Purpose: Revocation instant and reason exist exactly for revoked sessions.
Credential hash is exactly one SHA-256 digest.

constraints.Physical definition: CREATE INDEX human_sessions_principal_state_idx ON public.human_sessions USING btree (principal_id, state)
constraints.Purpose: Supports counting and listing a principal's sessions by state.

constraints.Physical definition: CREATE INDEX human_sessions_provider_session_idx ON public.human_sessions USING btree (provider_session_id)
constraints.Purpose: Supports back-channel logout by provider session identifier.

constraints.Physical definition: CREATE UNIQUE INDEX human_sessions_token_hash_key ON public.human_sessions USING btree (token_hash)
constraints.Purpose: One session per cookie credential; supports lookup by credential hash.
